article_title: Integrating Cognitive Linguistics Insights into Data-Driven Learning: Teaching Vertical Prepositions
citation: Kilimci, A. (2017). Integrating cognitive linguistics insights into data-driven learning: teaching vertical prepositions. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 13(2), 681-719. https://www.jlls.org
title: BNCweb-based DDL concordance instruction (CPDL) for vertical prepositions
description: The CPDL treatment combined BNCweb corpus consultation with PP-based cognitive explanations. BNCweb is described as "a web -based client program used for searching and retrie ving lexical, grammatical and textual data from the British National Corpus (BNC), which contains a 100 -million-word rich variety of annotated texts". Students received a three-hour DDL training session a week before instruction, then generated and interpreted concordance lines of the target prepositions, matching discovered senses to the PP polysemy networks. The control group instead used only print or electronic dictionaries on the same fill-in-the-blank materials.
requirements: A prior training session familiarizing students with corpus query techniques and concordance interpretation
A technology-enhanced room with projector, wireless connectivity and high-speed internet
constraints: The article notes DDL by itself may not suffice for teaching preposition senses, since corpus collocates alone do not explain the motivated semantic network
target_learners: second-year Turkish university students of English
target_learning_goals: learning the distinct senses and uses of the vertical prepositions over, above, under and below
examples: Students ran a first concordance of 50 lines with over in the middle, classified collocates by sense, and matched senses to the polysemy network handout
key_sources: Kilimci, A. (2017). Integrating cognitive linguistics insights into data-driven learning: teaching vertical prepositions. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 13(2), 681-719. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1159243

article_title: Adaptation of the Multi-Concept Multivariate Elo Rating System to Medical Students Training Data
citation: Erva Nihan Kandemir, Jill-Jênn Vie, Adam Sanchez-Ayte, Olivier Palombi, and Franck Ramus. (2024). Adaptation of the Multi-Concept Multivariate Elo Rating System to Medical Students' Training Data. The 14th Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK '24). https://doi.org/10.1145/3636555.3636858
title: BNE (Banque nationale d'entraînement) medical training platform dataset
description: The BNE is a national French digital learning platform used by over 8,800 medical students across all French universities annually, which also administers exams for all medical faculties. Its 2020-2021 training-period dataset comprises 8,616 users, 357,317 questions, 31 medical specialties, and 26,772,424 attempts, with user-question sparsity of 0.99 and 1.05 attempts per user, meaning students almost never re-attempt questions. Questions average 1.58 specialty tags, making it a multi-knowledge-component dataset; the mock final ECN exam subset covers 372 questions across 28 specialties with 3,172,546 interactions.
requirements: Analysis required pre-processing: removal of questions with fewer than 100 interactions (79.11% of unique questions removed) and binarization of question ratings
constraints: Use of the platform for training is optional, so learning occurring outside the platform was uncontrolled
Direct access to the official ECN exam is unavailable; only a mock exam in mid-March can be used for external validation
target_learners: Medical students across 42 French universities, 1st to 6th year, preparing for the ECN final exam
target_learning_goals: Training and mock examination across 31 medical specialties, emphasizing generalization rather than memorization of specific questions
examples: Students can tailor training by choosing question types and medical specialties, simulating and practicing for a wide range of medical exams according to their preferences and needs
key_sources: Erva Nihan Kandemir, Jill-Jênn Vie, Adam Sanchez-Ayte, Olivier Palombi, and Franck Ramus. (2024). Adaptation of the Multi-Concept Multivariate Elo Rating System to Medical Students' Training Data. The 14th Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference (LAK '24). https://doi.org/10.1145/3636555.3636858
